intro: のみ is the written, official だけ: a hard line around one item, the language of signs, notices, rules and formal writing. It says "this and nothing else" with a positive verb, exactly as だけ does, but it has none of だけ's chatty or "as much as" uses.

skills.rule: Use のみ for "only" in signs, notices, rules and formal writing; it keeps the verb positive like だけ, and casual speech uses だけ instead.
skills.explain:
のみ follows a noun, a number or a verb and limits it: 会員のみご利用いただけます (for members only), 当日のみ有効 (valid on the day only), お支払いは現金のみとなります (payment by cash only). It can follow other particles (平日にのみ) or simply replace them (平日のみ). After a verb, Vるのみだ means "all that remains is to V": あとは結果を待つのみだ.

XのみならずYも means "not only X but also Y" and is the formal version of だけでなく. It is common in news and essays.

The verb stays positive. With a negative verb the negative applies to the limited item: 会員のみ入れません means members are the only ones who cannot enter. のみ has no "as much as" sense, so できるのみ and 好きなのみ do not exist. In conversation it sounds stiff; a friend says ちょっとだけ待って, never ちょっとのみ.
patterns: [noun] のみ となります / 有効です  (notices)
[verb dictionary form] のみだ  "all that is left is to ..."
X のみならず Y も  "not only X but also Y"

examples.jp: 会員[かいいん]{のみ}ご利用[りよう]いただけます。
このチケットは当日[とうじつ]{のみ}有効[ゆうこう]です。
examples.en: This ticket is valid on the day only.

examples.jp: お支払[しはら]いは現金[げんきん]{のみ}となります。
準備[じゅんび]は終[お]わった。あとは結果[けっか]を待[ま]つ{のみ}だ。
examples.en: The preparations are done. All that remains is to wait for the result.

examples.jp: この問題[もんだい]は日本[にほん]{のみ}ならず、世界中[せかいじゅう]で起[お]きている。
examples.en: This problem is occurring not only in Japan but all over the world.

contrast.note: Same meaning, different register. だけ fits everything from chat to business; のみ fits signs, rules and writing. Only だけ has the "as much as" use (できるだけ, 好きなだけ).
しか also means "only" but needs a negative verb: 現金しか使えません. のみ takes a positive one: 現金のみ使えます. Never combine のみ with a negative to mean "only".
ばかり means "nothing but, all the time", often with a complaint: 文句ばかり言う. のみ just states the limit, with no judgement.

mistakes.bad: ねえ、ちょっと{のみ}待[ま]って。
mistakes.good: ねえ、ちょっと{だけ}待[ま]って。
mistakes.note: のみ is formal and written. In speech, and always with ちょっと or 少し, use だけ.

mistakes.bad: できる{のみ}早[はや]く提出[ていしゅつ]してください。
mistakes.good: できる{だけ}早[はや]く提出[ていしゅつ]してください。
mistakes.note: "As ... as possible" is always できるだけ. のみ has no "as much as" meaning.

mistakes.bad: このエリアは関係者[かんけいしゃ]{のみ}入[はい]れません。
mistakes.good: このエリアは関係者[かんけいしゃ]{のみ}入[はい]れます。
mistakes.note: For "authorised staff only", the verb stays positive. With a negative it says staff are the only people who cannot enter.

skills.tip: Would you see it on a sign, a ticket or in a rulebook? のみ. Said to a person face to face? だけ.
